IO&E Database Instructions

Find out how to search the publication library, browse by category, follow clinical trials, and maintain publication records.

The Interventional Oncology & Embolization (IO&E) Database brings together a curated publication library, PubMed discovery, and ClinicalTrials.gov monitoring. Use it to prepare for internal discussions, get familiar with a clinical topic, or locate original references for a Medical inquiry.

The View only label indicates that you can browse the collection. Editor sign-in is for colleagues who maintain the shared database.

1. Find a publication in the Library

Library search and filters. Select Clear to reset the filters.

1. Open Library. Search by title, author, country, or a term that might appear in the findings.

2. Narrow the list with All Products and All Categories. If the list is empty, remove a filter or try a broader term.

3. Open a publication to review the available details, such as the abstract, findings, or notes. Follow the article link to read and cite the original source. Full-text access depends on the source and your access permissions.

Example. For an internal discussion on Y-90 dosimetry, search for dosimetry, narrow by product if relevant, and open the original paper to confirm the microsphere type, study population, and dosimetry approach.

Library search and category filters

Choose a category for your question

Main categoryWhat it describes and where to start
IndicationDisease or tumor type. Try Indication › HCC, Lung Cancer, or Renal Tumor.
Evidence TypeStudy design or publication type. Try Evidence Type › Retrospective Study, Randomized Trial, or Systematic Review & Meta-analysis.
Clinical TopicThe clinical question. Try Clinical Topic › Safety, Efficacy, or Patient Selection.
TechniqueHow a procedure is planned or performed. Try Technique › Y90 Dosimetry, Mapping & MAA, or Cryoprotection.

A main category groups related subcategories. A record can be found through its Primary Category and its Secondary Tags. For example, a study tagged Technique › Y90 Dosimetry can appear when you select either Technique or Technique › Y90 Dosimetry.

Browse from a main category to a subcategory

1. In Library, select a main category in the category strip. Use More main categories… if the category you want is outside the visible chips. The strip then shows the selected group and its subcategories.

2. Select a subcategory such as Safety. You can also choose the same entry directly from All Categories. The strip and dropdown are two ways to select the active category.

3. Add All Products, a year, region, country, or a keyword to narrow the results. For example, choose Clinical Topic › Safety and Cryoablation, then type lung. Open a result and check which tag matched.

4. To step back, select the main category again or choose All in the strip to remove the category selection. Use Clear to reset the category, other filters, and both search boxes.

Choose the right search box

Standard search finds text stored in the Library record, including title, authors, country, results, findings, and tags. Start with a distinctive word or short phrase. It does not scan PDF text.

Smart search is useful for discovery. Try the built-in lung cryoablation example. Verify the study and its details before using the result. Use the product and category filters when you need an explicit restriction.

When results are sparse, remove a filter or shorten the text. A paper may be tagged under Dosimetry or Technique › Y90 Dosimetry, so try both the legacy label and the newer hierarchy when relevant.

Worked Library searches

Y90 glass dosimetry. Select Y90 Glass and enter dosimetry in the standard search. Broaden to Y90 (All) to include other microsphere groups. A Y90 Both label can indicate that both types are mentioned. Check the study design before calling it a head-to-head comparison.

DC Bead in HCC. Select DC Bead and enter HCC. Try hepatocellular if you need a different search term. For a broader treatment question, use TACE / DEB-TACE (All) and confirm which product each study actually evaluated.

Lung cryoablation safety. Clear the previous filters and use the lung cryoablation example in Smart search. Scan the matches, then open a record to check the indication and whether safety outcomes were reported. Switch between Table and Cards to show the available views.

How to adjust the results

If your first search is too broad, add a category that matches your question. For example, select Indication › HCC for disease focus or Technique › Y90 Dosimetry for planning methods. You can select one active category and combine it with a product filter and search text.

When comparing several publications, use Table to scan rows and sort with available column headings. Use Cards to read individual entries with more space. Clear Smart search if you want to return to ordinary sorting.

Read a publication record

Results contain the reported study outcomes and numbers. Key Findings summarize the takeaways. Open the original article for endpoints, denominators, follow-up, and limitations.

Check Review Status before relying on a summary. AI Draft still needs manual review. Journal Impact Factor (JIF) is a journal-level metric. Use the JIF year shown and assess the individual study from its methods and results.

For full text, follow the available PMC, PDF, or folder link. When a folder opens, use the recorded file name to locate the PDF.

2. Explore the collection in Dashboard

Open Dashboard to see how the curated collection is distributed across products, years, and topics. Use it to orient yourself before searching. The counts describe the publications included in this database.

Read the Dashboard panels

Overview shows total publications, PMC free full text, and records with a journal impact factor. By Product, By Year, and the category and country summaries show the makeup of the curated collection.

A publication can have several categories. Use category counts to see coverage without adding them to estimate the number of distinct papers. Select Export Excel + Dashboard to download the publication list and dashboard summary.

3. Find additional papers in PubMed Updates

PubMed Updates. Choose a literature stream and date range, or search by article title.

1. Open PubMed Updates and select a literature stream. For example, choose Cryoablation only.

2. Select Last 30 days to check for recent papers. To look up a specific article, enter its title or a few words from it and select Search title (all dates). Select Clear title to return to a broader search.

3. Open the PubMed record to verify the citation and find full-text options. If the paper would be useful to the team, send the title, PMID or DOI, and a short reason to the database owner.

Choose a PubMed search

Recent literature. Choose All IO&E, Y90 only, Cryoablation only, or DC Bead only. Select Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, or enter a day count and click Search custom days.

Known paper. Enter the complete title or a distinctive title phrase in Title / title keywords (optional). Select Search title (all dates). A date button can narrow the title query. Select Clear title before returning to topic discovery.

Access. The PMC FREE badge points to PubMed Central availability. Open the original record to confirm access and citation details.

4. Find and follow trials in Clinical Trial Monitor

Clinical Trial Monitor. Set the search scope, update period, and geography before searching.

1. Open Clinical Trial Monitor, choose a search scope, and optionally enter a topic, condition, sponsor, or device. Select Search Trials.

2. Refine the results by recruitment status or geography. For a regional search, choose APAC site involved and open the registry record to verify the specific countries and site-level status.

3. Select a trial’s NCT number to open its ClinicalTrials.gov record. Check the eligibility criteria, study locations, recruitment status, and last update there.

4. Star a trial you want to revisit and select View Watchlist to see starred records. Rerun the search when you want to check for changes. The first search establishes a baseline for comparison. Later searches can flag new or changed records.

Example. To find APAC studies in hepatocellular carcinoma, search HCC, apply APAC site involved, and review the locations in each registry record. If the search is too narrow, try hepatocellular carcinoma or broaden the scope.

Search the registry or filter results

Use the top toolbar to choose the search scope, update window, and geography before selecting Search Trials. To include older records, switch Updated in 90 days to Any update date and run the search again.

Use the lower row to narrow trials already loaded by NCT ID or text, status, phase, product, site geography, or monitoring state. Clear resets this results row. Export CSV downloads the results. Check the registry record before acting on status or APAC labels.

If you get stuck

What you seeWhat to try
No resultsClear filters, use fewer terms, or search by an exact title or NCT number where applicable.
The paper is missing from LibraryTry PubMed Updates or search PubMed directly.
Full text is unavailableOpen the source record and check publisher, institutional, or open-access options.
Trial search failsRetry from the hosted database. If it still fails, search ClinicalTrials.gov directly.
You spot a missing record or a correctionSend the article title, PMID, DOI, or NCT number to the database owner with the suggested change.

Use the original publication or trial registry when citing evidence or confirming details. Follow the established Medical process for external inquiries.

Editor sign in and publication entry

Editor sign-in controls from the v7.6 interface.

1. Ask the database administrator to provision your website account and authorize the same email for editor access. If you need a password reset, contact the administrator.

2. Open the database and select Editor sign-in. Enter your own Email address and Website password, then select Sign in.

3. Confirm that the header shows Editor or Admin and the Add Publication button is available. If the header still shows View only, ask the administrator to check the email authorization. If the shared database failed to load, reload before starting any edits.

Add a record manually

1. In Library, search for the title or a distinctive phrase first. Compare the PubMed or DOI link if you find a possible duplicate. Open the existing record’s edit control for a correction.

2. Select Add Publication. Enter the exact Title and four-digit Year. Complete Country when you can verify the study location, then add Authors, Journal, and the PubMed / DOI URL. For a journal with a verified registry entry, confirm the populated Journal Impact Factor and JIF Year.

3. Choose the Product from the paper. Use the brand-unconfirmed TACE option when the paper does not establish the brand. Add the verified Results, concise Key Findings, and relevant study limitations in Notes.

4. Set Review Status to AI Draft for automatically generated content until it has been manually checked. Review any content suggested by Auto-extract Findings against the source before marking the record Reviewed or Final.

Import an article from PubMed

Open PubMed Updates, find the paper, and select Import to Database. Check the prefilled citation, article URL, and PMC ID where available. Verify any suggested country, product, results, or tags before saving. If a paper is already in the Library, edit its existing record.

Create and manage categories as an editor

Add a main category

1. Sign in as Editor or Admin. From Library, click Manage Categories in the header or Manage in the category strip.

2. Scan existing main categories and their children for the same topic. Enter the new name in Main category and leave Optional subcategory empty. Click + Add Category.

3. Confirm Category added and verify the new entry in the manager. If the category already exists, use the existing label.

Add a subcategory to an existing main category

1. In Manage Categories, locate the parent and select + Add subcategory under it. Enter the child name and confirm. Alternatively, fill in the existing parent’s exact name under Main category, enter the child under Optional subcategory, and select + Add Category.

2. For example, if the team needs a new technique label, choose the existing Technique parent and add the agreed child name. The viewer will see it under Technique with the other techniques.

3. To create a parent and child together, fill in both fields before clicking + Add Category. For an existing category, use the pencil or the subcategory name to rename it and the × to remove it. Review affected records before renaming or deleting a shared label.

Apply the new category to a publication

1. Open Add Publication or edit an existing record. Select the new category from Primary Category if it describes the main focus, or from Secondary Tags if it describes another part of the paper.

2. Save the record and wait for the shared-save confirmation. In a separate viewer session, open Library, find the category in the strip or All Categories, and confirm the paper appears.

An added category can be empty until an editor applies it to a publication. If the tag is missing from the form, close and reopen the form after confirming the category was saved.

Tags and full text access

Choose one main topic and add secondary topics in the publication form.

1. Choose one Primary Category that reflects the central question of the paper. Then use Secondary Tags to add other relevant topics, one at a time. Check the selected tags in the form before saving.

2. For a lung cryoablation paper focused on safety, for example, choose the closest existing safety category as the primary category. Add the lung indication and study design as secondary tags if supported by the paper.

3. Use Manage Categories for changes to the shared category list. Check existing terms before adding a new category. Edits to the shared taxonomy can affect how colleagues find publications.

Choose how colleagues will open the full text

Where the full text is availableWhat to enter
PubMed CentralEnter the PMC ID (for example, PMC followed by its digits). Keep the citation link in PubMed / DOI URL.
OneDrive, SharePoint, or an authorized direct PDFPaste the file-level URL into PDF Link (optional). Use Direct PDF Link or Auto-detect from fields as appropriate.
Shared folder with an existing folder linkEnter the exact PDF File Name, including .pdf. Use PDF in Folder. Readers open the folder and locate the file by name.
Hard copy, request, or paywallSelect the matching Full Text Status and add a useful location or access instruction in Full Text Note / Location.

Add a OneDrive or SharePoint PDF link

Open the file in the approved shared location and copy its file link with access for the intended internal audience. Paste the link into PDF Link (optional). After saving, open the record and test its link with viewer-level access. If readers see an access request, check the file’s sharing permissions with the owner.

Set PDF Folder changes the shared folder fallback. Use it when the team’s common folder needs updating. For an individual paper, paste the link in PDF Link (optional).

PDF File (manual upload) lets you select a PDF inside the form. In v7.6 the shared save strips the uploaded file data, so use a file link or PMC ID for persistent viewer access.

Save verify and troubleshoot

Saving controls. The header button changes with the current save state.

Confirm the record is shared

1. Select Save now & close when you finish editing. You can also use Save now in the header. The initialized shared database can auto-save after you pause once the form has a title and valid year, so work on approved records.

2. Wait for Saved ✓ · Changes are saved to the shared database. Then search for the record again in a separate viewer session. Verify the title, product, tags, review status, and the citation and full-text links.

3. If Retry save appears, read the status before trying again. Use Export unsaved draft before reloading or signing out. If someone else saved a newer revision, coordinate with them or the administrator and reapply your changes to the current record. Avoid restoring a whole backup over their updates.

Editor quick checks

SymptomWhat to check
Add Publication is missingVerify Editor or Admin appears and the database loaded. Ask the administrator to check authorization for that exact email.
Paper does not appear in a viewer sessionConfirm shared save succeeded, reload the viewer, and clear Library filters.
OneDrive opens for the editor onlyCheck the file-level link and permissions using the intended viewer account.
A PDF was selected but viewers cannot open itAdd a persistent PDF Link or PMC ID, then verify from the viewer record.
Imported findings or tags look wrongCheck the original publication, edit the record, and confirm the corrected version is saved.

Contribution details. When suggesting a publication or correction, send the title and DOI, PMID, or NCT number, with a short explanation of what to add or change. Use the established Medical process for external inquiries.

Interface illustrations and editor workflows are based on the October v7.6 build. The sign-in and shared-save steps were checked against the saved interface and its code.

What this monitor tracks—and how to use it
  • Automated: recruitment status, phase, enrollment, sponsor, study dates, locations, interventions, results availability, and registry update date.
  • APAC results filter: use “APAC site involved” to narrow the trials already loaded, without running a new ClinicalTrials.gov search.
  • Change detection: new records plus changes in status, enrollment, completion date, locations, phase, or results posting versus your previous refresh.
  • Watchlist: click ☆ to save a trial, then use “View Watchlist” to retrieve your starred trials later. It creates a saved shortlist; it does not send automatic email alerts.
  • Recommended review: weekly for recruiting or competitor activity and monthly for completed trials and newly posted results.

Editor sign-in

Use your publication website password. If you need an account or forgot your password, contact the administrator.

Manage editors

Authorize a colleague’s email to let them add, edit, and delete publications and categories.

Manage products

Products in use cannot be deleted. Reassign their publications first. Y90 N/A is the required default.

The product will appear in the Add/Edit publication form and product filter.
